We have three templates returned. The first one (reaction_id 733) seems to be the sulfonamide formation: retro_smarts_template: '[O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]'

So applying this template to our target molecule should give precursors: sulfonyl chloride (Cl-S(=O)(=O)-aryl) and an aniline (NH2-aryl). The product is our sulfonamide.

We need to apply this template to the target SMILES to get all possible precursors. Use apply_template with template_id? We need template ID. The result includes template_hash but not ID. Possibly template_id is the reaction_id? Or we can use the retro_smarts_template directly? The apply_template tool expects template_id, not SMARTS. We might need to retrieve template by ID using get_template, but we don't have ID. Maybe the template ID is the hash? Not sure.

But perhaps we can use apply_template with the retro_smarts_template string? The tool expects template_id, but maybe it can accept SMARTS? Unclear.

Alternative: we can manually deduce precursors: For our target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

The sulfonamide nitrogen attached to aromatic ring (the first phenyl). The sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl with a vinyl-phenyl-amine substituent.

Thus the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2 (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The amine precursor would be aniline with methyl substituent: Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 (para-methyl aniline). So precursors: ['ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2', 'Cc1ccc(N)cc1'] but need proper SMILES: Chlorosulfonyl aryl: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2 . The amine: Cc1ccc(N)cc1 (or Cc1ccc(N)cc1). The nitrogen is primary amine.

Check if any other possible mapping (maybe the sulfonyl chloride could be on other aryl). But template may also allow swapping roles? The template has two fragments: sulfonyl chloride attached to aromatic carbon (c:4) and amine attached to aromatic carbon (c:6). In our product, the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (c:4) and amine attached to first phenyl (c:6). So only one combination.

Thus answer list: [['ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2', 'Cc1ccc(N)cc1']]

But need to ensure SMILES format: For sulfonyl chloride, chlorine attached to S: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CNc3ccccc3N)cc2 . That's valid.
